A champion of the delicious contemporary rogue-lite wave, Gungeon is a giant pool of CONTENT to dive into. The gameplay is similar to Nuclear Throne (or Touhou, the waifu-filled game pretty much every bullet-hell shooter can be compared to) but with much more gun and ability variety, and more focus on individual room clearing and dodging than on killing tons of enemies. Gungeon is a slow-paced game that still feels satisfying but can start to drag around the one hour mark. There are perhaps too many unlockables, especially considering how many guns are borderline useless end-game, but the amount of stuff there is to do means even when you die early every run you'll still be having fun and unlocking stuff.

Honestly used to love this game, but after 100 hours I truly realized why I got tired of it: It's slow as fuck. Runs can take almost an hour to complete and wether this game is fun or not imo relies a lot on rng. Even though you can probably beat the entire game with a default wep(that isnt blasphemy), just with sheer skill, would it really be fun? I know its not really the only game that suffers from this (TBoI and Nuclear Throne are 2 of my favourite rogue-lites/likes), but in others that do, items/weapons arent as uncommon. Otherwise the game has interesting synergies and characters, a cool story, but the gameplay is way too slow for my liking.

Mostly I have 1 important thing to say, and I'll get to that in a second. First, I just want to point out that this game is really well made, and super fun, and I'm kinda bad at bullet hell, so just know that none of my critique is based on the fact that I'm bad at it.

What I want to say is this: Gungeon is pretty far-off from something like Binding of Isaac in terms of the item synergy mechanics at the core of its roguelite gameplay. That confusing sentence is not a quality assessment, just an observation. In my limited time I've found that Gungeon does not supply you with infinitely compounding item effects during each run, but rather, a pretty tight load-out that you assemble from random items, and the shops, that consists of a few powerful weapons, and a few discrete (often non-synergistic) powerups/relics that assist your damage output but don't greatly change the way you play.

It's a subtle difference. So subtle you might just think I'm out to lunch, but I find it very noticeable. I came to this from games like Isaac and Slay the Spire, and was disappointed in the lack of emphasis on compiling wacky synergies. That is absolutely a, "to each their own," situation, and I don't hold it against Gungeon that it does things differently, but it isn't quite what I, personally, look for in a roguelite.

This is by far one of the most genuinely fun games in my library. Of the 20 or so hours I have logged on it so far, half of those hours were just me plunging into the gungeon again and again, just shooting shit and having fun. Only recently did I realize the amount of depth this game had to it; the NPCs, the story, the secrets. Now that I have a goal in mind, I'm having so much more fun playing this. I almost find myself confused by all the people who complain that this game is too hard; it's part of the experience. Die and die again until you know the patterns and the flow of the game. The variety of weapons, items, and enemies in this game is incredibly large for some indie pixel title. These devs know what they're doing with a video game.
In all honesty, I wish there was some sort of *substantial* DLC for this game. I would eagerly pay a little bit more for extra content; I feel like this game has a lot of potential for longevity in the market.

I just hopped out of another round and I gotta say... There is so much creativity with the weapons and enemies! The flavor text is humorous and the care and attention to detail in all of assets (art, sound, etc) is truly top notch! And the animations... You can really tell the team enjoyed putting this gem together.

One of my favorite things of all, though, is that the developers show that they understand what its players are after. The game is designed to *NOT* waste your time. All pickups conveniently gather to your character after each room is completed, teleport jumps ensure that you don't have to retread areas of the level previously covered, and yes, they even include an arrow at the edge of the screen to indicate where the last remaining enemy may be wandering around. Little touches that keep the experience focused on having "just one more run".

A refreshing experience all around, dodgeroll is definitely a new favorite developer for me!

This one is a bit of a gem, and I'd never have known about it had it not been for a certain Drummer of an 8-bit variety back during a charity livestream, and I thought it looked like the coolest thing ever. The best way I can summarize this game is Dark Souls with guns attained through RNG. Is it hard? It can be, but once you get good, it turns into a run-and-gun shooting gallery of a host of fun gun and bullet themed goons that are all based on some type of gun related pun. This is one of those games you'll need to try and fail at to get better, you're not getting through this entire game on your first try, unless you're absolutely god-tier with the controls and get lucky quite a lot. Easily worth the cash if you're looking for a challenge.

Enter the Gungeon is a fun game which combines the core gameplay of The Binding of Isaac, the variety of interesting weapons of Dead Cells, and a sense of humor that reminds me strongly of Swords Comic. It's definitely a difficult game and can border into frustrating, but I can also attest from personal experience that it's a game you can have fun being bad at.
EDIT: One quick warning. It looks like there's a remote co-op mode. There is not. My brother paid full price buying a second copy of this game after playing for a while through family sharing, specifically so that we could do co-op. Then we actually tried it, and found out that all I could actually do is watch his game by streaming and not actually join in.

Enter the Gungeon's difficulty might have you making several deposits into the swear jar... but it is also charming and engaging enough to give you hundreds of hours of gun-slinging, dodge-rolling, secret-finding fun.

I thought having 100%'ed and 100+ hour'd another bullet-hell game would've gotten me a headstart, but the fact was that I started from scratch again, as I failed stage/chamber 1 for many times in the early runs. Getting gud was extremely fun here regardless of that, as over 100+ hours later I managed to do all of the achievements and even had more with extended difficulty such as cursed run, which with slightly proper luck, can be manageable without broken luck.

admittedly, some of the starter characters can be quite crap to play with, especially without enough unlocks and decent quality drops, this can put a lot of starters off. the investment in playing time to unlock enough items and other stuffs for EtG to start being really fun, I think it was about 5-10 hours of gameplay.

Do you feel calm under pressure?

Do you feel like you do well even when overwelmingly disadvantaged?

Do you like dying?

if you answered no to any of these thats okay, because soon you will answer yes if you play this enough. I sure have played this a lot this week so let me explain how I feel about it.

Cons: Can feel like it doesn't matter how much skill you have, sometimes the odds are stacked (just like life).
Also the STUPID LEAD MAIDEN GAAAHHH... i hate it.. Also sometimes one can feel like they arent given enough instruction as to what things are and instead of having a sense of mystery and intrigue, for me at first I was just annoyed by the in game secrets.

Pros: Controls are snappy, they do just what you want, and if you die its usually because of you.
Music is so good... I annoy my wife after I play by whistling the tunes for hours after stopping.
The art is done well, the characters have good well... character. The humor is impeccable, and I could totally see many dads and non dads alike think its witty. Needless to say the pros FAR outway the cons and I would definitely recommend it.
